grades.quote: To ensure that certain implicit reads are ordered only after writes to the same memory locations, software must execute specific fence or cache-control instructions defined for this purpose (such as the FENCE.I instruction defined in Chapter 5).
grades.reason: The passage is the general RISC-V memory overview. It mentions FENCE.I only as an example of an instruction software uses to order implicit instruction fetches after writes. It never says whether a local FENCE.I synchronizes instruction fetch on other harts, so it gives only limited background.
